investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-28T00:51–00:58Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs is exhausted or the allocatable count is zero), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 128–145 seconds, the eval runner timed out before any agent lifecycle state could be observed, leaving all required evidence fields empty and causing all three remote-agents checks to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots are in use by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') and is the most evidence-supported cause.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are simultaneously at capacity, creating a hard scheduling deadlock with no preemption path.

TERTIARY — The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource count on the two eligible nodes may have been reduced (e.g., node cordoned, resource quantity patched to 0, or node-level peer-pod daemon unhealthy), making the resource appear exhausted even if no pods are actively consuming it.

QUATERNARY — A cluster autoscaler or node provisioner that would normally add kata-capable nodes failed to trigger or complete in time, leaving the fixed pool of 6 nodes as the only scheduling candidates.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking All Remote Agent Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-28T00:53–00:58Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata.peerpods.io/vm pods because 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource label. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that every new remote-agent pod request is immediately Unschedulable. No preemption is possible because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers the pod creation that stalls; the probe then times out before any agent identity or state can be captured, producing an empty evidence object and violating the expected-output contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=149033 (≈149s), well above the pod-stuck threshold of 145s cited in the failure message, confirming the probe waited the full timeout before failing.

sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable scheduler message, latencyMs=133822, failed before remote-agent-state started — indicating the scheduling block was already present when the eval sequence began.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=150375, failed after remote-agent-state — confirming the block persisted across the entire eval window.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1905 as the first substantive step; a scheduling failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: contract at line 264 requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none of which can be populated if the agent pod never starts.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval-provisioned pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message across all three sibling checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes carry, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before the resource check even applies.

Tertiary — stuck or leaked remote-agent pods from a prior eval run holding VM slots without releasing them: if cleanup (withCleanup in the runner) failed on a previous cycle, orphaned pods could be occupying the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval runs plus any production workload sharing those nodes.

Secondary: A GitHub Actions runner quota, billing limit, or branch protection rule may have blocked the scheduled workflow run that would have refreshed the snapshot.

Lower likelihood: A misconfiguration mismatch — the registry entry (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) sets staleAfterMinutes=360 while the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482) enforces max=300 — could cause the eval to fail even when the workflow runs on its normal cadence if the workflow interval exceeds 300 minutes.

Lower likelihood: The published snapshot URL (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json) may be serving a cached or previously committed static file rather than a freshly workflow-generated one, if the GitHub Pages deployment step was bypassed.
